context: Two architecture students planning a presentation on bamboo as a building material

cues.t: Part 3. You will hear two architecture students, Laura and Finn, planning a presentation on bamboo as a building material. First you have some time to look at questions 21 to 25.
Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 25.
Finn, can we plan the bamboo presentation? It's only ten days away.
Sure. I was thinking we should begin by explaining how we came to choose the topic.
Wasn't it your trip to Indonesia? You came back full of ideas.

No, that was afterwards. We'd already chosen it by then. What started it was that television documentary about the school in Colombia. And remember, Dr Marsh was trying to persuade us to do recycled concrete instead.
That's right, she was. Okay. Then we need to set out the advantages. Everyone says bamboo is cheap.

It is where it grows. But once you've shipped it to Europe, it isn't cheap at all. And whether it looks good is a matter of taste. For me, the point that matters most is how fast it grows. You can harvest it after three to five years, and a tree needs thirty at least.

Agreed, we'll lead with that. I'd like to say something about strength as well. I'd read that it can be as strong as steel when you pull it, so that didn't surprise me. What did surprise me was how much it varies from one species to another. Some kinds are no use for building at all.
Yes, we should warn people about that. And then the difficulties. I suppose the damp climate here is the big one.

I don't think so. Properly treated bamboo copes with rain perfectly well. And you can always train builders to work with it. The real obstacle is that the building regulations here don't mention bamboo at all. So you can't get a design approved, and nobody will insure it.
Good point. Now, how shall we divide it up?
I'll do the introduction. And since you did the laboratory work, perhaps you could explain the test results.
I'd rather you did the figures, to be honest. You explain numbers more clearly than I do. I'll describe the case studies. I've got all the photographs.
Fine by me.
Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 26 to 30.
Now listen and answer questions 26 to 30.
So tell me about the case studies. Which buildings have you got?

Five. The first is Riverbend School, the one from the documentary. What I like about it is that no construction company was involved. The parents and neighbours put it up themselves, without being paid, over two summers.
That's a good story. And the footbridge?
Sanda Bridge. It's forty metres long, and two years after it opened there was a major earthquake. Concrete buildings nearby collapsed, and the bridge was still standing.
Impressive. What about the café you mentioned?

The Lotus Café. That one's a warning, really. To save money, the owners used bamboo that hadn't been treated, and within three years beetles had eaten into the main posts. Half of it had to be pulled down.
We should definitely include that. And the hostel?
Mountain View Hostel, in Austria. It looks wonderful, and it was finished on time. But all the bamboo had to be imported, and the final bill was almost double the original budget.
So it went well over budget. And the last one?
The Harbour Pavilion. It took twice as long to build as anyone expected. But last year it was given an international prize for design, which is probably why people have heard of it.
Great. That gives us a good mix of successes and failures.
That is the end of Part 3. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

items.stem: How did the students first become interested in bamboo?

options.A: Finn visited a bamboo building abroad.
options.C: They saw a programme about it.

items.stem: What does Finn think is the greatest advantage of bamboo?
What surprised Laura about the strength of bamboo?

options.A: It can be as strong as steel.
options.C: It decreases as the plant gets older.

items.stem: According to Laura, the main barrier to building with bamboo locally is
What will Finn do in the presentation?

groups.instruction: What does Finn say about each of the following buildings?
groups.limit: Choose FIVE answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–F, next to Questions 26–30.

options.B: It was built by unpaid local people.
options.C: It was finished ahead of schedule.

questions.explain:
答案是 C。Finn 說 What started it was that television documentary about the school in Colombia。
同義轉換：television documentary ＝ a programme。陷阱：A 是 Laura 的印象，但 Finn 說 that was afterwards，印尼之行是選定題目之後的事；B 錯在老師其實希望他們做再生混凝土。
questions.quote: No, that was afterwards. We'd already chosen it by then. What started it was that television documentary about the school in Colombia.

questions.explain:
答案是 A。Finn 說 For me, the point that matters most is how fast it grows。
陷阱：B 是 Everyone says，但運到歐洲之後 it isn't cheap at all；C 的外觀是 a matter of taste（見仁見智）。題目問 greatest advantage，對應 the point that matters most。
questions.quote: For me, the point that matters most is how fast it grows.

questions.explain:
答案是 B。Laura 說 What did surprise me was how much it varies from one species to another。
陷阱：A 的「和鋼一樣強」她早就讀過，that didn't surprise me；C 整段都沒提到。題目問 surprised，要分清楚「不意外」和「意外」的兩件事。
questions.quote: What did surprise me was how much it varies from one species to another. Some kinds are no use for building at all.

questions.explain:
答案是 A。Laura 說 The real obstacle is that the building regulations here don't mention bamboo at all。
同義轉換：regulations don't mention bamboo ＝ lack of official standards。陷阱：C 是 Finn 的猜測，被 Laura 否定（I don't think so）；B 錯在工人 you can always train。
questions.quote: The real obstacle is that the building regulations here don't mention bamboo at all.

questions.explain:
答案是 C。Finn 說 I'll describe the case studies. I've got all the photographs。
陷阱：A 是 Laura 要做的；B 是 Laura 建議 Finn 做的，但他說 I'd rather you did the figures，把數據推回給 Laura。別人的建議不等於最後的決定。
questions.quote: I'd rather you did the figures, to be honest. You explain numbers more clearly than I do. I'll describe the case studies.

questions.explain:
答案是 B（由當地人無償興建）。Finn 說 The parents and neighbours put it up themselves, without being paid。
同義轉換：without being paid ＝ unpaid；parents and neighbours ＝ local people；put up ＝ build。
questions.quote: The parents and neighbours put it up themselves, without being paid, over two summers.

questions.explain:
答案是 F（撐過地震）。Finn 說大地震後 Concrete buildings nearby collapsed, and the bridge was still standing。
同義轉換：was still standing ＝ withstood。
questions.quote: Concrete buildings nearby collapsed, and the bridge was still standing.

questions.explain:
答案是 D（被昆蟲蛀蝕）。Finn 說 beetles had eaten into the main posts。
同義轉換：beetles（甲蟲）屬於 insects。陷阱：他提到 To save money，但這是用了未處理竹材的原因，不是 A（超出預算）。
questions.quote: To save money, the owners used bamboo that hadn't been treated, and within three years beetles had eaten into the main posts.

questions.explain:
答案是 A（超出預算）。Finn 說 the final bill was almost double the original budget，Laura 總結 So it went well over budget。
陷阱：it was finished on time 是「準時」完工，不是 C 的「提前」完工（ahead of schedule）。
questions.quote: But all the bamboo had to be imported, and the final bill was almost double the original budget.

questions.explain:
答案是 E（獲得國際獎項）。Finn 說 last year it was given an international prize for design。
同義轉換：prize ＝ award。陷阱：It took twice as long to build 和 C（提前完工）正好相反，所以 C 是本題組沒用到的選項。
questions.quote: But last year it was given an international prize for design, which is probably why people have heard of it.
